Action Plan:
1) Suspected acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk. Plan: emphasize oral rehydration and fluid replacement (Diarolyte) over plain water; maintain clear fluids initially and progress to soft diet (soup, mash) as tolerated; avoid heavy foods until symptoms settle. Continue regular Paracetamol for fever/pain as needed; avoid alcohol. Advise 48-hour follow-up or sooner if dehydration or fever persists/worsens. If symptoms persist beyond 48 hours or dehydration develops, arrange further evaluation.

2) Monitoring and follow-up. Plan: reassess in 1–2 days to ensure symptom resolution and hydration status; call back sooner if unable to keep fluids down or if there are signs of dehydration (e.g., reduced urine, dizziness, fainting).

3) Education and safety netting. Plan: avoid dairy if vomiting persists; continue hydration and gradual diet advancement; likelihood of viral gastroenteritis explained; no antibiotics prescribed at this time.

4) Documentation of consent. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Note: A COVID-19 vaccine suitability assessment was not documented in this consult.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: several days of extensive watery diarrhea with cramping abdominal pain; episodes abundant and frequent (nearly hourly when awake); associated nausea and occasional vomiting (milk-related). Feels hot/febrile; not sleeping well.
- Onset/duration: symptoms began about 3 days ago (Monday/Tuesday); persistent and not improving.
- Diarrhea: watery stools, no blood reported.
- Abdominal pain: crampy, midline, intermittent, rating about 6–7/10 when present; pain is not constant.
- Nausea/vomiting: present; vomiting occurs, in particular with milk.
- Feverish symptoms: feeling hot and burning sensation; no measured fever.
- Urinary: decreased frequency but not absent; otherwise not specified.
- Diet: last solid intake around lunch today; still able to drink, but fluids largely pass through.
- Hydration: attempting to drink water, but fluid loss appears rapid.
- Allergies: none reported.
- Medications: occasional Paracetamol; no regular medications.
- Past medical history: generally fit and well; no chronic illnesses noted.
- Family history: father with colon cancer (currently described as in third stage, not fully clarified); not sure of exact prognosis.
- Social history: lives with mother and sister in Central London; works in government office; smokes socially; consumes alcohol socially (beer on some occasions; weekends/monthly occasions).
- Other: no travel history or identifiable trigger; brother recently had similar symptoms for about five days but currently improving.

Objective:
- No physical examination findings or vital signs documented in transcript.
- No laboratory results or imaging reported.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral, secondary dehydration risk)
   - Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis.
   - Differential diagnoses: none explicitly documented; viral gastroenteritis presumed.
   - Investigations: none ordered at this visit; monitor for dehydration; escalate if not improving.
   - Treatment: oral rehydration with Diarolyte; clear fluids now and soft diet (soup, mash) as tolerated; continue Paracetamol for fever/pain; avoid alcohol; avoid dairy if vomiting persists; gradual dietary advancement as tolerated.
   - Referrals: none.

2) Dehydration risk monitoring (implicit from plan)
   - Assessment: dehydration risk due to high stool frequency and fluid loss.
   - Investigations: none ordered; reassess hydration status if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment: maintain hydration; follow-up within 1–2 days or sooner if dehydration signs develop.
   - Referrals: none.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate), physical examination findings, weight, baseline labs or stool studies, formal medication reconciliation, documented hydration status.
- Internal conflicts: none identified; no contradictory statements detected in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: generally clear; some filler language and minor colloquialisms; no major inaudible segments detected.
